The white cell and platelet lineages are not expanded, which distinguishes this secondary erythrocytosis from a myeloproliferative polycythemia. A cell-intrinsic contribution of HIF-2-alpha within erythroid progenitors has also been proposed.

nodes.description: Recurrent exon 12 missense variant at Gly537.
The first identified ECYT4 allele (c.1609G>T), replacing the small conserved glycine with a bulky tryptophan in the oxygen-dependent degradation domain.

A heterozygous germline missense variant in EPAS1 alters a residue in or near the oxygen-dependent degradation domain of HIF-2-alpha, close to the prolyl-hydroxyl-acceptor Pro531 (reported changes include G537W, G537R, M535V, M535I, M535T and P534L). The variants are gain-of-function: they impair recognition of HIF-2-alpha by the PHD2 hydroxylase and by the von Hippel-Lindau protein. Functional characterisation across these alleles shows a common endpoint of impaired degradation despite distinct effects on PHD2 and VHL interaction.

evidence.reference_title: Current views on the role of HIF-2α in the pathogenesis and syndromic presentation of pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma.
evidence.snippet: HIF-2α evades steady-state hydroxylation by the prolyl hydroxylase type 2 (PHD2), which accelerates von Hippel-Lindau (VHL)-mediated proteasomal degradation. In this situation, HIF-2α is stabilized and can translocate to the nucleus

nodes.description: HIF-2-alpha is the direct effector of the disease, so HIF-2-alpha inhibition is a mechanistically targeted therapy. Belzutifan, a HIF-2-alpha inhibitor, has been reported to normalise the haemoglobin in EPAS1-associated polycythemia without further phlebotomy. Carriers with a causal EPAS1 variant in the hydroxylation region are candidates for this treatment. The evidence is case-level: the 2026 management review of JAK2-unmutated erythrocytosis states that the role of HIF2A inhibitors remains unclear, so this is a mechanistically rational therapy whose place in care is not yet settled.

In humans with HIF-2-alpha gain-of-function, pulmonary hypertension is accompanied by increased cardiac output, heart rate and ventilation; in the knock-in mouse modeling the first human variant, pulmonary hypertension develops with high penetrance alongside the erythrocytosis.
